subject: Request: Temporary deferment of multi-region redundancy / conditional RTO/RPO commitments
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane.park@borealbank.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+contracts@borealbank.com
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Temporary deferment of multi-region redundancy and RTO/RPO request

Alex —

Thanks for the demo last week. We like Redwood's latency profile, but our finance team needs to stagger the cost of full multi-region warm standby for the first six months.

Request: would Redwood consider a conditional carveout where Boreal remains single-region (us-west) for up to 6 months while Redwood provides documented RTO/RPO commitments for failover, a playbook for rapid activation, and an interim SLA that nudges toward the standard multi-region SLOs (we understand it won't be identical)?

We attached our internal risk assessment (boreal-warmstandby-risk-assessment.pdf). High level asks:
- A defined RTO target for region outage scenarios (we're proposing 60 minutes).
- RPO expectations and replication cadence (we propose async snapshots every 5 min).
- A mitigation checklist Redwood will own while we defer the warm standby build.
- An economic offset or credit tied to the delayed warm standby activation.

Can you loop in legal/ops on Redwood's side and send back a short term-sheet or testable commitments? We need something we can attach to procurement.

Appreciate it —
Jane
VP Ops, Boreal Bank

Attachment: boreal-warmstandby-risk-assessment.pdf (pdf, 420KB)
From: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
To: Jane Park <jane.park@borealbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2025 11:05:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary deferment of multi-region redundancy and RTO/RPO request

Jane —

Thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the risk assessment. We're sympathetic to the phased-cloud approach — a lot of customers start this way. We can offer a conditional carveout with defined guardrails so your procurement team has something concrete. High-level proposal (for discussion):

- Interim commitment: Redwood will commit to an operational failover playbook plus a testable RTO target of 60 minutes for the specified region outage classes, with caveats around catastrophic cloud provider-wide outages.
- RPO: We can guarantee a maximum RPO of 5 minutes using continuous async replication / incremental snapshots. We will document replication lag metrics and expose them via the Console.
- Activation cadence: Warm-standby activation window will be "on-call-to-traffic" in 60 minutes once Redwood initiates failover. We'll provide a runbook and a weekly drill cadence option.
- Compensation: We'll provide a credit equal to one month of Dedicated capacity (pro-rated) if activation exceeds the committed RTO in a customer-initiated real-world event. This credit is limited to the deferment window (max 6 months).

We need to loop in Legal (cc'd) to translate this into a short addendum. Questions for you: is the 6-month window fixed from the date of contract signing, and do you require periodic verification drills during the window?

I'll attach a one-page term sheet and a short checklist for the mitigation responsibilities.

—Alex
Product Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-temp-carveout-term-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32KB)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai, Jane Park <jane.park@borealbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2025 15:48:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary deferment of multi-region redundancy and RTO/RPO request

Thanks Alex — tagging Legal & Reliability. A couple operational clarifications from infra:

- "60 minute RTO" needs to be scoped to failures at the availability zone or single-region level where control-plane functionality is available; provider-wide blackout (e.g., region+control-plane outage) is excluded. We'll add explicit exclusions and runbook steps.
- We'll commit to replication metrics: 99th percentile replication lag <= 5 minutes measured at the KV snapshot boundary. We'll surface metrics and an alert channel to Boreal's PagerDuty/ops distribution.
- During the deferment period Redwood will perform one internal failover drill (read-only failover) at week 8 and will offer up to 2 joint drills on request (additional joint drills may incur a services fee).

Legal note (Naomi) — we should keep the credit mechanics simple and capped. Also propose a signoff on the risk assessment and a requirement that Boreal disables certain high-risk config changes (we'll list them) while on the single-region plan.

Kimberly
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Temporary deferment of multi-region redundancy and RTO/RPO request

Looping in from the cloud ops advisory side — a couple practical points from our runbooks that matter to the RTO guarantee:

- If Boreal runs >70% of steady-state traffic in the primary region, activation risk increases; recommend mitigating by routing lower-priority workloads to a queuing tier during failover to reduce peak load.
- Ensure your DB connector uses tx-safe retries; otherwise async replication consistency at scale can add seconds of stall during cutover.

We recommend a joint smoke test (10% traffic) as part of the drill so both parties verify observability and rollback behavior. Happy to support as part of the two joint drills.

—Matt
Senior Cloud Resilience Engineer, Infraserve
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 23 Dec 2025 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Final: Short addendum for BR-4271 (temporary single-region carveout)

Jane / team —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed this with Reliability and Legal. Below is the agreed short-form addendum language we'll attach to the master services agreement for BR-4271. If this looks good we can circulate a DocuSign and target execution before 12/31. Key points:

1) Duration: temporary carveout effective from signature date for up to 6 months.
2) Scope: Customer remains in single-region (us-west) production while Redwood provides
   - Operational failover runbook and 60-minute RTO target (exclusions for provider-wide control-plane outages).
   - RPO commitment: async replication with 5-minute max lag (99th percentile).
   - Monitoring: replication and lag metrics exposed to customer Console and a designated alert channel.
3) Drills: Redwood to conduct one internal read-only drill (week 8) and up to two joint drills on request.
4) Compensation: If actual failover activation in a customer-impacting event exceeds 60 minutes, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 1/30th of the customer's monthly committed capacity per incident (capped at the pro-rated deferment credit in the term sheet).
5) Preconditions: Customer agrees to follow the mitigation checklist during the deferment (listed in attachment).
6) Termination: Full multi-region obligations resume at the earlier of (a) end of the 6-month window or (b) customer request to enable warm standby.

Please confirm acceptance or provide final edits by EOD 12/30 so we can route to DocuSign. Once countersigned we'll schedule the week 8 read-only drill and open the alert integration ticket.

Best —
Naomi Feldman
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
